Praktisch 7-stappenplan voor ondernemers: Practical 7-step plan for business owners to translate external cyber threats into decisions, actions and measurable outcomes. Includes owners and KPIs.
Waarom dit nu prioriteit is Volgens de N: Why this is a priority now According to the NCSA progress report (Open Overheid), the Netherlands actively participates in European cyber exercises such as Cyber Europe 2021 — a clear signal that cyber threats are not only technical problems but governance- and supply-chain-wide risks that also affect small and medium-sized businesses. For entrepreneurs this means: do not wait for an incident, but build a simple closed improvement loop that links external signals to strategy, budget, processes, people and risk.
De gesloten verbeterlus: van signaal naa: The closed improvement loop: from signal to learning An effective approach is used as a repeatable cycle: signal → context → consequence → decision → action → result → learning. Below is a concrete 7-step plan you can apply immediately, including who makes the decision, which action owner you appoint and which metric you use to monitor progress.
Stappenplan: 7 concrete stappen met eige: Action plan: 7 concrete steps with owner and metric 1) Collect signals - What: collect internal and external signals (phishing reports, irregular access attempts, news about supplier incidents, advice from NCSC / NCSA). - Owner: IT/security contact (or external IT partner if you don’t have internal IT). - Metric: number of reported security signals per week and percentage of reports with sufficient information (basic quality score).
Hoe veranderende externe signalen je str: How changing external signals affect your strategy and money - Signal to strategy: if a national exercise or sector warning shows that supply-chain attacks are increasing, your strategy should shift from ‘reactive patching’ to ‘supplier resilience’: stricter contract clauses, supplier audits and budget for substitution or redundancy. - Money and priority: translate risk into a simple business case format: what is the maximum downtime (in hours/days) and what is the expected likelihood? Use that as an argument to free up budget for concrete measures (MFA, backup tests, supplier audit). No precise guarantees — but a reasoned choice based on probability x impact.
Mensen en processen: wie doet wat anders: People and processes: who does what differently? - Create simple RACI charts per measure (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) so no one thinks ‘ICT’ handles it alone. - Invest in one concrete training per quarter and a short playbook for who to call in incidents (customers, insurer, authorities).
Risico’s en controleerbare uitkomsten (v: Risks and verifiable outcomes (example decision) Example decision: “Within 30 days: mandatory implementation of MFA for all external logins and 90% of internal accounts.” - Owner: IT manager (implementation) and CFO/MT (budget and verification). - Verifiable outcome metric: % of accounts with MFA activated within 30 days. This directly reduces the risk of account compromise; the exact reduction depends on incident data and is measured in step 6.
Praktische tips om direct te starten - B: Practical tips to start immediately - Start small: choose one critical business process (e.g., invoicing) and work through the 7 steps in one month. - Use existing sources such as the NCSA reports for signals and exercises to validate priorities. - Create one dashboard with 5 KPIs: alerts/week, % critical assets patched, % MFA-coverage, backup-restore success, incidents per quarter.
Conclusie Cyberdreigingen vereisen een b: Conclusion Cyber threats require a governance approach that translates external signals into concrete business decisions and measurable actions. Work in short cycles, appoint owners and use simple KPIs. Start today with a small, manageable pilot and scale based on real results and learning.

2) Context maken: welke bedrijfsprocesse: 2) Create context: which business processes does this affect? - What: link signals to critical processes (invoicing, customer data, production lines).
Beschrijf gevolgen per proces (beschikba: Describe consequences per process (availability, confidentiality, integrity). - Owner: COO or process owner together with IT. - Measurement point: number of critical assets/processes identified and prioritized (e.g., list of top-5 assets with impact score).
3) Consequentie-inschatting en risico-ev: 3) Consequence estimation and risk evaluation - What: estimate possible impacts in business and financial terms (downtime, revenue loss, fines, reputational damage). Use a simple likelihood*impact scale (low/moderate/high). - Owner: CFO + risk owner. - Measurement point: completed risk evaluation per asset (likelihood x impact class) in the risk register.
4) Beslissing: prioriteren en toewijzen: 4) Decision: prioritize and assign - What: choose which risks you will address this cycle (e.g., need for MFA, patching, backups, supplier investigation, insurance). - Decision owner: executive board or MT (clear escalation for high risks). - Expected outcome (verifiable): approval of budget and priorities, plus named action owners for each measure.
5) Actie uitvoeren (sprintgerichte uitvo: 5) Execute actions (sprint-based execution) - What: concrete measures in short sprints (30/60/90 days). Examples: mandatory MFA for external access, daily patch cadences for critical systems, backup restore testing, phishing simulation and minimal hardening of supplier handovers. - Action owner: IT manager or appointed implementation manager; HR for training; procurement for supplier control. - Measurement point: concrete implementation statistics (e.g., % users with MFA within 30 days, patch-compliance % within 14 days, backup restore test passed yes/no).
6) Resultaat meten - Wat: meet of de act: 6) Measure results - What: measure whether the action reduces the risk: number of incidents, time-to-detect, time-to-recover, number of successful phishing attempts, supplier compliance. - Owner: security lead + business owner of the process. - Measurement point: set of KPIs, for example time-to-recover in hours, number of security incidents per quarter, percentage of suppliers with basic security requirements completed.
7) Leren en herijken - Wat: evalueer de: 7) Learn and recalibrate - What: evaluate the outcomes, update risk assessments, adjust policies and budgets, and close the loop by monitoring new signals. - Owner: MT (responsibility for governance) with security lead as rapporteur. - Metric: number of policy updates and improved risk scores; re-evaluation within 90 days.
Als je hulp wilt opschalen: POWERHOUSE k: If you want to scale up assistance: POWERHOUSE can act as the engine to bring together signals from different sources and automatically support the closed loop — but keep decisions, priorities and approvals with the executive board. Technology helps organize information; people make the decisions.
Gebruik Cyberdreigingen niet als papiere: Do not treat Cyber threats as a paperwork checkbox: assess the actual situation, test the criteria and record the chosen action.
